headline: High: shared filesystem writes and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between marketingskills and plano.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marketingskills can read/write filesystem and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” while plano is an out-of-process gateway that can ingest upstream content. That creates a plausible shared-file or handoff path where attacker-controlled content from one agent can influence the other. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF the pair shares any workspace, cache, or handoff file, then injected instructions can cross from one agent to the other.
IF plano forwards upstream text into prompts without provenance filtering, then marketingskills output can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Separate per-agent workspaces and temp directories.
Strip or label untrusted content before passing outputs between agents.
Add provenance tags to every handoff artifact.
Disable automatic file-based handoffs between the pair.
requires-engineering: enforce content-safety filters at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: marketingskills touches marketing content and product marketing context and can write files; plano has broad network egress and handles logs/metrics/traces. If they share files or context, sensitive marketing material can flow into plano’s outbound requests or telemetry. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred and escalated only to medium.
conditions: IF both agents read from the same directory or config bundle, then marketing content can be exposed to plano.
IF plano includes logs, traces, or prompt context in outbound API calls, then shared content can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive marketing files out of shared directories.
Review plano egress destinations and disable unnecessary telemetry.
Use separate credentials and API keys per agent.
Redact marketing context before any cross-agent transfer.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on shared artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marketingskills supports multiple instances and can write the filesystem, while plano has broad egress but no subprocesses and no multi-instance support. If both are pointed at the same mutable files or config, concurrent edits can overwrite each other. The profiles do not show locking, so the conflict is plausible in default shared deployments.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory, then file clobbering or config drift can occur.
IF an orchestrator launches multiple marketingskills instances alongside plano without locks, then race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Make shared config read-only during runs.
Run only one writer per resource at a time.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed to build on shared context, and plano is an AI gateway that can route or forward model outputs. That makes it plausible that one agent’s output becomes the other’s input without verification, which can propagate hallucinations or bad marketing decisions. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF plano forwards marketingskills output into downstream prompts or actions, then errors can cascade.
IF marketingskills content is treated as authoritative by plano, then incorrect facts can be amplified.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse of outputs.
Require citations or source links for factual claims.
Limit downstream actions to drafts only.
Log and review cross-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. marketingskills is open-source and unverified; plano exposes logs/metrics/traces and broad egress, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict. Because the evidence is insufficient, this remains a low-confidence, low-severity gap rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF either deployment processes regulated data and the operator routes it through plano without a DPA or residency controls, then compliance risk increases.
IF retention settings differ between shared logs and source files, then deletion/export obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Document data classes handled by each agent.
Check retention settings for logs and artifacts.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review vendor terms and residency before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
